name: Manali
tagline: Snow peaks, apple orchards and the rushing Beas river.
whenBlurb: Come March to June for green valleys and open passes, or October for apple harvest, Kullu Dussehra and the first snow; skip the July-August monsoon landslides.

ourTake.lede: Manali splits sharply between the overrun main town and the quiet, beautiful Old Manali and the villages up the valley, so stay in the latter. Use it as a base for the high passes and the Spiti or Sissu side rather than the town's tourist strip. Timing is everything: the Rohtang and Atal Tunnel access, the snow, and the road to Spiti all depend on season, so plan around what's open.
ourTake.comeIf: You want mountains, orchards and river valleys a short hop from Delhi.
ourTake.skipIf: You want to avoid crowds in peak season, or want a beach.

guide.lede: Where to stay, what to do, where to eat, and where the night goes, grouped by price, every address earned by a name worth trusting.

items.name: The Himalayan
credentials: Recognised design/boutique castle resort, Victorian Gothic Revival, at 2,003 m above Manali town
Featured in Condé Nast Traveller; long-listed among Himachal's leading five-star/boutique stays
items.description: A Victorian Gothic Revival castle of turrets and spiral staircases, set among apple and cherry orchards with the snow peaks beyond, the most characterful address in the valley.

items.name: Span Resort & Spa
items.area: Manali (Baragran, ~12 km north on the Beas)
credentials: World Luxury Hotel Award (2017)
Healing Hotels of the World member (2016–2017)
Bloomberg TV, Best Luxury Resort in Himachal Pradesh (2015); one of the oldest large luxury resorts in the valley, est. 1981
items.description: The valley's grande dame, a riverside five-star of walnut orchards and deodar since 1981, still the byword for a settled family stay on the Beas.

items.name: Manuallaya – The Resort Spa in the Himalayas
credentials: Five-star spa resort (Ambassador Resorts), TripAdvisor Travelers' Choice
Recognised for its TVA Spa, temperature-controlled indoor pool and specialty dining (Kibber, D'Jong, Café Jardin)
items.description: A contemporary five-star spa resort on the hillside above Manali, open lawns, an indoor heated pool and long valley views.

items.name: The Allure Grand Resort
items.area: Manali (Bahang, ~5 km north, riverside on the Beas)
credentials: Recognised five-star riverside resort on the Beas (official standing)
Consistently high-rated on TripAdvisor for service and setting
items.description: A polished modern riverfront five-star on the Rohtang road, a pool with a mountain view, gardens and an outdoor fire.

items.name: LaRiSa Resort Manali
items.area: Naggar (Haripur, ~20 km south on the Kullu–Naggar–Manali road, riverside)
credentials: Property of Larisa Hotels & Resorts, recognised riverside luxury resort near Naggar
Noted for its own orchards and organic kitchen gardens, spa and private orchard dining
items.description: An apple-orchard retreat on the Beas below Naggar, its own organic gardens, a spa and an outdoor pool, quietly away from the Manali crowds.

items.name: The Sonaugi Homestead
items.area: Naggar / Sonaugi (~20 km south of Manali, above the valley)
credentials: Hand-built by Italian architect Eris Binda in traditional Kath-Kuni (stone-and-wood) construction, operated by Banjara Camps & Retreats
Responsible Tourism India listed heritage-style homestead
items.description: A five-room stone-and-timber house hand-built in the native Kath-Kuni style, ringed by deodar forest and apple orchards, architecture and silence rather than resort polish.

items.name: Hadimba Devi Temple
items.description: A four-tiered pagoda of cedar and stone from 1553, dedicated to Bhima's wife from the Mahabharata, set in the deep Dhungri cedar forest where the light falls in shafts. The most atmospheric temple in Manali and, in a light snowfall, quietly cinematic for a family morning.

items.name: Dhungri Cedar Forest walk
items.description: The ancient deodar grove that cradles the Hadimba temple, thick with towering cedars several centuries old. A slow, cool wander here is the antidote to Mall Road crowds, and a good private-guide walk for a multi-generation group.

items.name: Old Manali
items.description: The original village up the Manalsu stream, all apple orchards, stone-and-timber homes and slow cafes above the newer town. It has the boho river-cafe scene the honeymoon set loves, yet keeps a genuine Himachali village texture underneath.

items.name: Manu Temple
items.description: A modest pagoda temple in Old Manali dedicated to the sage Manu, held by legend to be the only temple to him in India. Worth the climb through the village lanes for the setting and the quiet, more than the shrine itself.

items.name: Vashisht Hot Springs & Temple
items.description: An old stone village across the Beas with natural sulphur hot springs feeding bathing tanks beside the Vashisht and Rama temples, the water long believed to soothe the skin. Rustic and crowded, but the geothermal steam against cold mountain air is a genuine novelty.

items.name: The Mall Road
items.description: The pedestrian spine of Manali, lined with Kullu-shawl shops, Tibetan handicrafts, wool and cafes. Best walked at dusk for an easy evening stroll; a private guide can steer you past the tourist tat to the real shawl and pashmina houses.

items.name: Gadhan Thekchhokling Gompa
items.description: Manali's principal Tibetan monastery, built in 1969 by refugees, with vivid murals, a large Buddha and a small carpet-weaving unit and market at the gate. A serene, colourful stop a short walk off Mall Road.

items.name: Himalayan Nyingmapa Gompa
items.description: The bright yellow-roofed monastery near the Mall, its inner hall presided over by a golden Buddha with rows of prayer wheels and a calm courtyard. A quick, quietly beautiful counterpoint to the busy streets.

items.name: Tibetan Market
items.description: The warren of stalls around the monasteries selling prayer flags, singing bowls, turquoise-and-silver jewellery and woollens. Good-humoured haggling and the best place to pick up small Tibetan pieces.

items.name: Van Vihar Nature Park
items.description: A 51-acre grove of soaring deodars right on Mall Road, with shaded paths and a small lake for pedal-boating. The easiest green breather in town, ideal with young children or grandparents in tow.

items.name: Manali Club House
items.description: An HPTDC amusement zone on the Manalsu stream with boating, go-karting, zip-lining, a ropeway and indoor games. Frankly touristy, but a reliable half-day of easy fun for families with kids.

items.name: Jogini Falls trek
items.description: A gentle 3 km walk from Vashisht through apple orchards and pine to a roughly 150 ft cascade with a small Jogini Mata shrine at its foot. A short, rewarding morning hike that even less-active family members can manage part of.

items.name: Nehru Kund
items.description: A cold natural spring beside the highway, fed from the high Bhrigu Lake and named for Jawaharlal Nehru, who drank from it on his Manali stays. A brief, pretty roadside pause on the way up towards Solang and Rohtang.

items.name: Solang Valley
items.description: The wide meadow-and-snow amphitheatre that is Manali's adventure hub, ringed by peaks and glaciers. Green and blossom-strewn in summer, a white playground in winter, and the single most photographed valley near the town.

items.name: Paragliding at Solang
items.description: Tandem flights off the Solang slopes with a pilot, from short 'joy' hops to longer high flights, roughly April to December. The view of the valley and the Beas from the air is the thrill most first-timers remember.

items.name: Solang ropeway (gondola)
items.description: A cable-car ride up the Solang slope for wide views over the meadows and, higher up, the snow line. The gentlest way for grandparents and children to reach the upper viewpoints without the crowds on foot.

items.name: Zorbing & snow play at Solang
items.description: Rolling downhill inside a giant transparent ball on the summer grass, plus ATV rides, horse rides and, in winter, sledding and snow-tubing. The easy, giggly adventure end of the spectrum for a family day out.

items.name: Skiing at Solang
items.description: Winter turns the gentle Solang slopes into North India's most accessible beginner ski runs, with skiing, snowboarding and snowmobiling from about December to February. Instructors and hired kit make it an easy first taste of the sport.

items.name: Atal Tunnel
credentials: World's longest highway single-tube tunnel above 10,000 ft (9.02 km, opened 2020)
items.description: The engineering marvel that punches under the Pir Panjal to link Manali with Lahaul in about ten minutes, once a treacherous half-day over Rohtang. Driving through it is itself a novelty, and it opens the once-cut-off Lahaul valley year-round.

items.name: Sissu
items.description: The first Lahaul village beyond the tunnel, on the Chandra river beneath the tall Palden Lhamo (Sissu) waterfall, with a placid lake and a starkly different high-desert light. The easiest taste of Lahaul, reachable as a comfortable day trip since the tunnel.

items.name: Sissu Waterfall (Palden Lhamo Dhar)
items.description: A tall glacier-fed cascade tumbling down the mountain wall across the Chandra from Sissu village, named for a Tibetan protector deity. A dramatic first sight of Lahaul, framed by the barren peaks the tunnel suddenly reveals.

items.name: Keylong & Jispa
items.description: The Lahaul district town of Keylong and the riverside hamlet of Jispa on the Manali-Leh road, ringed by monasteries, barley fields and glaciers. A quieter, more remote day out for travellers wanting Lahaul beyond Sissu.

items.name: Rohtang Pass
credentials: Access permit-gated (daily NGT vehicle quota); closed in winter and every Tuesday for maintenance
items.description: The classic 3,978 m snow pass, still the great Manali outing for snow, wind and Himalayan drama despite the tunnel below. Permit- and quota-gated and only open roughly May to October, so a private operator handling the paperwork is essential.

items.name: Gulaba snow point
items.description: The lower snow point on the Rohtang road, reachable without the Rohtang permit and reliable for snow play well into spring. A practical, hassle-free snow fix when the pass itself is shut or over-booked.

items.name: Naggar Castle
items.description: A 15th-century stone-and-timber castle above the Beas, once the seat of Kullu's rajas and now blending Himalayan kath-kuni craft with a heritage hotel and cafe on its terraces. The valley views from its courtyard are among the finest in the region.

items.name: Nicholas Roerich Art Gallery
items.description: The former home of the Russian painter-mystic Nicholas Roerich, now a gallery of his luminous Himalayan canvases set in gardens above the valley he loved until his death here in 1947. A cultured, unexpected stop that lifts a Naggar day well above sightseeing.

items.name: Kullu town & Raghunath Temple
items.description: The valley's administrative and spiritual heart, home to the 17th-century Raghunath temple whose deity presides over the famous Dussehra. A working town rather than a resort, best as a cultural stop en route to the shawl weavers or Bijli Mahadev.

items.name: Kullu shawl weavers (Bhuttico)
credentials: Kullu shawl carries a Geographical Indication (GI) tag
items.description: The Bhutti Weavers Cooperative, founded in 1944, where you can watch Kullu shawls and pattus woven on handlooms and buy directly at source. The most authentic place to acquire the region's signature craft, well beyond the Mall Road stalls.

items.name: Bijli Mahadev trek
items.description: A short but steep 3 km climb to a ridge-top Shiva temple at 2,460 m, famous for the tall staff said to draw lightning each year. The 360-degree panorama over the Kullu and Parvati valleys from the top is the real reward.

items.name: Manikaran Sahib
items.description: A revered gurdwara and temple complex on the Parvati river where scalding natural hot springs boil out of the ground, used to cook langar and for ritual bathing. The mix of steam, faith and the roaring river makes it one of the valley's most striking sights.

items.name: Kasol
items.description: The riverside village that anchors the Parvati Valley, with pine-shaded banks, Israeli cafes and a laid-back backpacker energy. A pleasant lunch-and-stroll base from which to explore the valley's temples and trails.

items.name: Tosh village
items.description: A cliffside hamlet at the head of a Parvati side-valley, with snow-peak views, guesthouse balconies over the gorge and a slow mountain rhythm. A worthwhile detour for the vista, framed here as scenery rather than for its cannabis notoriety.

items.name: Kheerganga trek
items.description: A demanding day's climb through forest and waterfalls to a high meadow with a natural hot spring and a Shiva shrine, one of the Himalayas' best-loved treks. Framed here as an experience to know of; the fit and well-guided can attempt it, most will admire it from below.

items.name: Malana village
items.description: An isolated ancient village on a side ridge, famous for its unusually self-contained culture, distinct customs and a democracy said to be among the world's oldest. Culturally fascinating and best understood from a distance and with a respectful local guide; visitors follow strict do-not-touch rules.

items.name: Great Himalayan National Park
credentials: UNESCO World Heritage Site (inscribed 2014, for outstanding biodiversity)
items.description: A vast UNESCO-listed wilderness of alpine meadows, glaciers and rare fauna spread across the Tirthan, Sainj, Jiwa and Parvati valleys. The serious naturalist's Himalaya, entered on foot with permits and guides for a genuine off-grid few days.

items.name: Tirthan Valley
items.description: A green, unhurried valley centred on Gushaini that is the gateway to the national park, known for trout fishing, riverside stays and forest walks. The quiet, upscale-slow-travel alternative to bustling Manali.

items.name: Jibhi
items.description: A tiny wooded village of timber cottages and a hidden forest waterfall, one of Himachal's most photogenic hideaways. A restorative base or day trip for travellers who want pine-scented calm over crowds.

items.name: Jalori Pass & Serolsar Lake
items.description: A 3,120 m pass with sweeping Dhauladhar and Pir Panjal views, from which an easy forest trail leads to the serene Serolsar Lake and its Budhi Nagin shrine. A rewarding high-mountain half-day from a Jibhi or Tirthan base.

items.name: Chehni Kothi tower
items.description: A centuries-old kath-kuni tower-fort of dry-stacked stone and timber, several storeys tall and still standing without cement or steel, reached by a short uphill walk. A striking piece of vernacular Himalayan engineering for the culturally curious.

items.name: Beas river rafting
items.description: White-water rafting on the Beas along the Pirdi-Jhiri stretch, with grades suiting first-timers and thrill-seekers alike, best from April to June and September to October. A classic Kullu-valley adrenaline hit that families can share.

items.name: Trout fishing on the Beas
items.description: Angling for prized Himalayan trout in the cold Beas and its tributaries around Katrain, Larji and Kasol, on HPTDC day permits. A calm, characterful pursuit, and the trout ends up on the dinner table.

items.name: Apple orchard visits
items.description: The Kullu Valley is India's apple heartland, and in the autumn harvest you can walk the laden orchards around Naggar and Katrain, picking and tasting at the source. A gentle, seasonal pleasure that grounds a trip in the valley's real livelihood.

items.name: Gushaini & the Tirthan riverside
items.description: The confluence hamlet where the Tirthan and Sainj rivers meet, the launch point for national-park treks and prized trout beats. A soothing riverside stop for a slow lunch or an overnight in a boutique fishing lodge.

items.name: Chandratal Lake
items.area: Spiti border via Lahaul, ~2 days from Manali
items.description: The crescent 'Moon Lake' at over 4,300 m near Kunzum Pass, a startling turquoise set against bare high-desert peaks. Deep in Spiti-Lahaul terrain, this is a hard-earned expedition rather than a day trip, and unforgettable for the intrepid.

items.name: Kunzum Pass
items.description: A 4,551 m prayer-flag-draped pass that is the gateway from Lahaul into Spiti, with a small hilltop temple and vast glacier views. A serious high-altitude drive, reached far more easily now via the Atal Tunnel route.

items.name: Johnson's Cafe
items.area: Manali (Circuit House Road, near Old Manali)
credentials: Legendary Manali institution est. 1997, India's first trout-speciality restaurant
The most-cited fine-dining name in Manali, part of Johnson's Lodge
items.description: The valley's original destination table, a garden of rustic wood and jazz, and the grilled Himalayan trout that made its name.

items.name: The Lazy Dog
items.area: Old Manali (Manu Temple Road, riverside on the Beas)
credentials: Widely regarded as Old Manali's oldest and best-known gastro-pub / riverside café
Cited across leading Manali dining round-ups for its riverside setting, cocktails and live music
items.description: Old Manali's original riverside gastro-pub, the Beas at your feet, live music by evening and a genuinely broad kitchen.

items.name: Cafe 1947
items.area: Old Manali (by the Old Manali bridge, riverside)
credentials: Long-standing, widely-cited Old Manali riverside institution
Known for wood-fired pizzas and its live-music evenings
items.description: The Old Manali institution by the bridge, wood-fired pizza and pasta with the Beas rushing past and live music after dark.

items.name: Casa Bella Vista
credentials: Long-running Old Manali institution, a Spanish-and-Indian-run café widely cited among the valley's best
Noted for its wood-fired pizzas, garden setting and library
items.description: A tiny Spanish-run café among the orchards, alfresco tables, a small library and honest Mediterranean cooking with a river view.

items.name: Drifters' Cafe
credentials: Long-standing, widely-cited Old Manali café, 'Drifters Cafe, Bar & Inn by The Hidden Tribe'
Known for its breakfasts, live acoustic nights and easy backpacker-to-family appeal
items.description: The beloved Old Manali breakfast room, eggs Benedict and Florentine, pancakes and waffles, board games and acoustic evenings.

items.name: Hotel bar nightcap
credentials: Johnson's Cafe bar (est. 1997) and the licensed bars of the five-star resorts (Span, Manuallaya, The Allure Grand)
items.description: A quiet drink by a fireplace, Johnson's bar in town, or the calm lounge bars of the riverside resorts, the most civilised late hour in the valley.

items.name: Old Manali café & live-music evening
credentials: The Lazy Dog and Cafe 1947, widely-cited Old Manali riverside gastro-pubs known for live music
The valley's principal evening scene, riverside cafés with acoustic and live sets
items.description: Manali's real night out, cocktails or cider by the river with an indie band playing, at The Lazy Dog, Cafe 1947 and their neighbours.

plan.heading: 4 days in Manali, done well
plan.lede: A day-by-day shape for the trip, the pace we would set. Your advisor books the flights and the rooms; the days are yours.

slots.label: Morning
slots.text: Arrive into the Kullu valley and settle at The Himalayan or a river-facing suite, then take a slow walk to the deodar-shaded Hadimba temple.

slots.label: Afternoon
slots.text: Wander Old Manali's lanes and the apple orchards along the Manalsu, unhurried.

slots.label: Evening
slots.text: Dinner at Johnson's Lodge café over trout and a bottle from the small European list.

slots.label: Morning
slots.text: Drive up to the Solang valley early, before the crowds, for the alpine air and views toward the Beas Kund ridge.

slots.label: Afternoon
slots.text: Continue toward the Atal Tunnel and Sissu for the Lahaul side, returning by late afternoon.

slots.label: Evening
slots.text: Quiet dinner in-house with a fire lit, or Drifters' Café in Old Manali.

slots.label: Morning
slots.text: Drive south to Naggar Castle, the old Kullu-raja stone-and-timber fort above the river.

slots.label: Afternoon
slots.text: Visit the Nicholas Roerich estate and gallery, then the Urusvati institute, among pine and mountain light.

slots.label: Evening
slots.text: Return to Manali; dine at The Corner House or your hotel.

slots.label: Morning
slots.text: Cross to Vashisht for the hot springs and the small stone temples, then coffee overlooking the valley.

slots.label: Afternoon
slots.text: A short forest walk to the Jogini falls before packing.

slots.label: Evening
slots.text: Early supper and departure, or a final night by the Beas.

items.name: Old Manali
items.description: The leafy, café-lined village above the town; best for atmosphere and calm.

items.name: Naggar / lower valley
items.description: Historic and quiet with the old castle and orchards; suits those wanting heritage and space.

items.name: Manali town (Mall Road)
items.description: The busy commercial centre; practical for logistics but best avoided as a base.

events.name: Kullu Dussehra (nearby)
events.note: The week-long valley festival at Kullu, when hundreds of village deities are carried in procession; the region's great event.

events.name: Winter Carnival, Manali
events.note: A cold-season festival of local culture, food and snow sports in the town.

events.name: Hadimba Devi Fair
events.note: A local temple festival at the atmospheric wooden Hadimba shrine among the cedars.

events.name: Spiti / high-pass access season
events.note: The window when the high roads over Kunzum and towards Spiti open; the reason to time a longer trip.

onGround.heading: On the ground
onGround.note: Base yourself in Old Manali or a quiet estate above the town rather than the crowded Mall; the Atal Tunnel now keeps the Lahaul side open through winter, and mornings are the window before afternoon traffic and cloud build up on the passes.

rows.label: Arriving
rows.value: Fly to Bhuntar (Kullu-Manali) airport, roughly two hours south, and continue by private chauffeur up the valley; most travellers instead take a private car from Chandigarh (about eight hours) or a helicopter charter direct to Manali when weather allows.

rows.label: Getting around
rows.value: A private car and driver is the only sensible way to move between Old Manali, Solang and the higher passes; the town centre and Mall Road are best on foot.

rows.label: Connectivity
rows.value: Jio and Airtel 4G is reliable in Manali town but thins out fast toward Rohtang and Atal Tunnel; download offline maps and expect no signal on the high passes.

rows.label: Money
rows.value: Indian rupee; cards work at hotels and larger restaurants but keep cash for local cafes, taxis and mountain stops; rounding up or ten percent is a gracious tip.

rows.label: Climate
rows.value: March–June is kind: alpine air, open passes, blossom in the valley. Avoid July–August (monsoon landslides shut the Chandigarh–Manali highway) and deep January snow unless you want it.

rows.label: Flights from India
rows.value: No jet airport at Manali. Fly Delhi–Bhuntar (Kullu, KUU) in about 75 minutes on a small ATR (IndiGo/Alliance/Star), then a 50km, ~1.5hr road transfer up to Manali; the strip is weather-sensitive and cancels often. The reliable UHNI move is Delhi–Chandigarh in business (Air India) then a 6–8hr private car north, or a helicopter charter. The Atal Tunnel now keeps the onward Lahaul route open year-round.

rows.label: Health & safety
rows.value: No vaccinations beyond routine. Very safe; roads are the real risk, insist on a seasoned mountain driver, not a self-drive. Manali town sits at ~2,000m, gentle, but if you push on to Rohtang/Atal Tunnel (~3,000m+) allow for thinner air. Tap water is not potable; stick to sealed bottled or filtered.

rows.label: Dining, veg & Jain
rows.value: Effortless for vegetarian and Jain, this is Himachal, largely vegetarian by default, and dhaba-to-hotel food is veg-forward. Pure-veg and Jain (no onion/garlic) is standard on request. Johnson's Cafe and the better hotel kitchens (e.g. Span, The Himalayan) handle refined vegetarian and North Indian well.
